topic: The Most Beautiful Equation: Euler's Formula and e^(πi) = -1
target_audience: University freshmen and advanced high school students interested in mathematics and physics.

sections.title: The Grand Reunion: Introduction to the Identity
lecture_lines: Behold the most beautiful equation in all of mathematics.
It unites five fundamental constants in a single identity.
Meet zero, one, e, i, and pi.
Geometry, calculus, and algebra converge in this expression.
Let's explore how these different worlds become one.
animations: Fade in the equation e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 in white (#FFFFFF) at the center.
Highlight '0' and '1' with a blue (#0000FF) scale-up pulse.
Highlight '\pi' with a green (#00FF00) scale-up pulse.
Highlight 'e' and 'i' with a yellow (#FFFF00) scale-up pulse.
The entire equation glows and then fades out.

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: The Nature of 'e' and 'i'
lecture_lines: e is the fundamental base of natural growth.
i is defined as the square root of negative one.
Multiplying by i rotates a number by ninety degrees.
animations: Display 'e' (#00FF00) and a vector growing along the x-axis.
Display 'i' (#0000FF) and rotate the vector 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
Show the text "i^2 = -1" as the vector rotates another 90 degrees.

sections.title: Prerequisite 2: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: The complex plane maps numbers in two dimensions.
Real numbers go horizontal; imaginary numbers go vertical.
Every point has a distance and a rotation angle.
animations: Draw the Real axis (#FFFFFF) and Imaginary axis (#FFFF00) with labels.
Plot point (2, 1) and label it "2 + i".
Move a small dot from (0,0) to (2,1) following the vector.

sections.title: The Secret of Imaginary Exponents
lecture_lines: Real exponents scale a value up or down.
Imaginary exponents do something different: they rotate.
The expression e to the i theta traces a circle.
Here, theta represents the angle of rotation.
Growth is transformed into continuous circular motion.
animations: Draw a grey unit circle (#555555) on the complex plane.
Display e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta (#FFFFFF) above the circle.
Animate a vector rotating from angle 0 to \theta.
Project a vertical line to the x-axis, labeled \cos\theta.
Project a horizontal line to the y-axis, labeled i\sin\theta.

sections.title: The Journey of π: Reaching the Destination
lecture_lines: Set the rotation angle to exactly pi radians.
Pi radians corresponds to a perfect half-circle.
We start at positive one on the real axis.
A half-circle rotation lands us at negative one.
Therefore, e to the power i pi is negative one.
animations: Start with a unit circle and vector at point (1, 0).
Rotate the vector 180 degrees counter-clockwise to point (-1, 0).
Display the identity e^{i\pi} = -1 (#FFFFFF) near the vector tip.
Transform the identity into e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 by moving terms.
Draw a glowing gold box (#FFD700) around the final formula.

sections.title: Conclusion: Synthesis and Impact
lecture_lines: This identity links exponential growth to circular rotation.
It underpins modern physics, signal processing, and waves.
Complexity simplifies into this one elegant truth.
animations: Synchronize the rotation of the vector with a traveling sine wave.
Display floating labels "Signal Processing" and "Quantum Waves" (#00FFFF).
Fade everything to leave e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0 in the center.
